questions.stem: What are the three components of the Human Development Index?
options: Education, health and income
Income, employment and inequality
Health, environment and income
Education, income and political freedom
questions.why: Education is measured by years of schooling, health by life expectancy, and income by GNI per capita at PPP.
whyNot: HDI excludes employment and inequality.
HDI excludes the environment.
HDI excludes political freedom.

questions.stem: How is the income component of HDI measured?
options: GNI per capita at purchasing power parity
GDP per capita at market exchange rates
Total GDP in US dollars
Median household income
questions.why: GNI rather than GDP, because GNI counts income accruing to residents wherever it is earned, which matters where profits leave the country.
whyNot: It uses GNI, and adjusts for purchasing power.
It is measured per head.
Median income is not used.

questions.stem: How is the health component of HDI measured?
options: Life expectancy at birth
Infant mortality
Doctors per thousand people
Public health spending per head
questions.why: It reflects nutrition, sanitation, clean water, health care access and safety all at once, and it is comparatively reliable to measure.
whyNot: That is a separate indicator.
That is one of the other named measures of development.
Spending is an input, not an outcome.

questions.stem: Which of the following best defines economic development?
options: An improvement in living standards and welfare, including health, education and freedom, as well as income
An increase in the real output of an economy
A rise in a country's exports
An increase in the size of the labour force
questions.why: Growth is a means; development is the end.
whyNot: That is economic growth.
That is export growth.
That is labour force growth.

questions.stem: Why does HDI use two education indicators?
options: Mean years captures the current workforce, expected years captures current provision and the future
One measures primary and the other secondary schooling
One measures male and the other female schooling
Two indicators are used to make the index harder to manipulate
questions.why: A country that has recently expanded schooling shows low mean years and high expected years, which tells you the direction of travel.
whyNot: Both cover the whole schooling span.
The index is not disaggregated by gender.
The reason is informational, not anti-manipulation.

questions.stem: Why does HDI use a geometric rather than an arithmetic mean?
options: A very poor score on one dimension drags the whole index down and cannot be offset by another
It makes the index easier to calculate
It allows negative values
It removes the need for a PPP adjustment
questions.why: A country cannot buy a high HDI with income alone, which is a deliberate design choice.
whyNot: It is slightly harder to calculate.
The dimension indices lie between 0 and 1.
The PPP adjustment is still applied.

questions.stem: Why is the income component logged before being scaled?
options: An extra $1,000 matters far more at low income levels, which is diminishing marginal utility
To make the index easier to interpret
To remove the effect of inflation
To convert the figure into a percentage
questions.why: Without it, very high incomes would dominate the index.
whyNot: It complicates rather than simplifies interpretation.
Constant prices handle inflation.
The scaling handles the range.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most important omission from HDI?
options: Inequality, so an average can conceal a wealthy minority and a deprived majority
Life expectancy, which is not included
Income, which is not included
Schooling, which is not included
questions.why: The environment and political freedom are the other major omissions, and the inequality-adjusted HDI exists partly for this reason.
whyNot: Life expectancy is the health component.
Income is the third component.
Schooling is the education component.

options: Life expectancy and mean years of schooling are stocks that move over decades
The data is only collected every ten years
The index is deliberately smoothed
Income per head rarely changes
questions.why: That makes it insensitive to recent policy, which is a real limitation for assessing a government's record.
whyNot: It is published annually.
No smoothing is applied.
Income per head can change quickly.

questions.stem: A country has high income per head but low access to clean water and few doctors. What does this show?
options: Income is not being converted into health provision, so the average conceals where the money goes
The income data must be inaccurate
The country must be at war
HDI cannot be calculated for the country
questions.why: Using several indicators together is what reveals this, which is why the specification names six additional measures.
whyNot: The data may be accurate and the pattern informative.
There is no basis for that inference.
It can be calculated.

questions.stem: What is the limitation of using the percentage of adult male labour in agriculture?
options: It excludes women's work, which is a serious omission in agricultural economies
Agriculture cannot be measured
It applies only to developed economies
It is identical to GDP per capita
questions.why: Some agriculture is also highly productive, so a high figure does not always indicate subsistence farming.
whyNot: Employment by sector is measured routinely.
It is most informative for developing economies.
It measures structure, not income.

questions.stem: Why is energy consumption per capita an imperfect development indicator?
options: Higher is not better environmentally, and it rewards inefficiency
It cannot be measured
It only applies to oil-producing countries
It is unrelated to industrialisation
questions.why: A country that becomes more energy efficient would appear less developed on this measure.
whyNot: It is measured routinely.
It applies to all countries.
It correlates with industrialisation, which is why it is used.

questions.stem: Why is access to mobile phones per thousand people used as a development indicator?
options: It captures communications and increasingly banking through mobile money
It measures the wealth of the richest households
It measures the quality of telecommunications regulation
It measures the size of the manufacturing sector
questions.why: Its limitation is that it counts devices rather than people, and many own several.
whyNot: It is a population-wide measure.
It measures access, not regulation.
It is unrelated to manufacturing size.

questions.stem: Why can growth occur without development?
options: Growth concentrated in a capital-intensive sector owned from abroad can raise GDP without improving health or education
Growth always reduces living standards
Development always precedes growth
GDP cannot be measured in developing economies
questions.why: That is why growth is a means and development is the end, and the distinction should open any answer in this topic.
whyNot: Growth usually raises living standards, but not necessarily.
They usually move together, in either order.
It is measured, with varying accuracy.

questions.stem: What is the right conclusion on whether HDI is a good measure of development?
options: Better than income alone, insufficient by itself, and best used alongside other indicators
The best possible single measure of development
Useless, because it omits inequality and the environment
Equivalent to GDP per capita
questions.why: It also depends what the comparison is for: it suits comparing basic living standards and not assessing sustainability or freedom.
whyNot: Its omissions are substantial.
It is a clear improvement on income alone.
It includes health and education as well as income.

questions.stem: Why is HDI data weakest where it matters most?
options: Statistical capacity is lowest in the poorest countries, which the index most needs to measure
The index is not published for poor countries
Poor countries deliberately misreport their data
Life expectancy cannot be estimated at all
questions.why: PPP conversions are also imprecise and revised, which adds further uncertainty.
whyNot: It is published for almost every country.
Capacity rather than intent is the general problem.
It is estimated, with wider margins of error.
